Reproducing Pagan et al. (2025) from dandiset 001550¶

Paper. Pagan M, Tang VD, Aoi MC, Pillow JW, Mante V, Sussillo D, Brody CD (2025). Individual variability of neural computations underlying flexible decisions. Nature 639, 421-429. doi:10.1038/s41586-024-08433-6. This attempt used the open access full text (PubMed Central PMC11903320, CC BY), with the Methods and the Extended Data legends.

Dandiset. DANDI:001550, version 0.260916.0811. The paper cites no DANDI version: its data statement points to a GitHub repository, and the dandiset was made later from the same behavioural files. This is the only published version, so it is pinned; the draft has the same 16,115 assets and size.

What the dandiset holds. The behaviour of 26 rats: 16,115 sessions in 11 protocols, each with a trials table (context, outcome, generative evidence strengths, and the time of every pulse) and, in some TaskSwitch6 sessions, optogenetic epochs. The electrophysiology (3,495 units) is not in it. Files are streamed from the archive: each file is read whole into memory and opened there.

Outside inputs. The paper's data repository Brody-Lab/flexible_decision_making_rats at commit 0ea8fdb7c56d755d99155171cc314dbbc24393ac: its per-session behavioural tables (to test the link to the dandiset), its trial counts and saved regression weights (as reference values), and its neural data and fitted per-neuron pulse kernels (for the neural claims, which the dandiset cannot test). Everything is fetched from GitHub at that commit, into memory.

import os
os.environ.setdefault("OMP_NUM_THREADS", "1")
os.environ.setdefault("OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS", "1")

import time
import warnings
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from scipy import stats

import taskswitch as ts

pd.set_option("display.width", 220)
pd.set_option("display.max_columns", 40)
pd.set_option("display.max_rows", 300)
warnings.filterwarnings("ignore", category=RuntimeWarning)

started = time.time()
assets = ts.asset_table()
task_assets = assets[assets.protocol.isin(ts.TASK_PROTOCOLS)].reset_index(drop=True)
results = ts.load_many(task_assets.url)
other_assets = assets[assets.protocol.str.startswith("TaskSwitch") & ~assets.protocol.isin(ts.TASK_PROTOCOLS)].reset_index(drop=True)
other_results = ts.load_many(other_assets.url, keep_bins=False)
print(f"dandiset {ts.DANDISET_ID} version {ts.DANDISET_VERSION}: {len(assets)} files; "
      f"read {len(results)} task sessions and {len(other_results)} other TaskSwitch sessions "
      f"in {time.time() - started:.0f} s")


def session_table(table, res):
    s = pd.DataFrame([r["session"] for r in res])
    return pd.concat([table[["subject", "protocol", "session", "date", "size"]].reset_index(drop=True), s], axis=1)


S = session_table(task_assets, results)
S_other = session_table(other_assets, other_results)
S["readable"] = S.missing.fillna("") == ""
S["selected"] = S.readable & (S.valid >= ts.MIN_VALID) & (S.hit >= ts.MIN_HIT) & (S.fsi >= ts.MIN_FSI)

dandiset 001550 version 0.260916.0811: 16115 files; read 15413 task sessions and 440 other TaskSwitch sessions in 66 s

Thirteen task sessions lack the result codes or a pulse column, and are left out of every count below. Where both exist, hit_history agrees with the outcome derived from result_history on every trial, so the outcome is taken from result_history, which every other session has. Some files store HistorySection_gammafreq_history, a signed strength, as an unsigned or 16-bit integer; in every one of them its values equal the float gamma_freq, so no sign was lost.

Pulse times lie within 0 to 1.3 s of the start of the pulse train, and there are about 52 per valid trial, the 40 Hz over 1.3 s of the Methods. The generative strengths take six values, plus 0 for the training stages that lack one feature. The pulse columns' description says seconds from the centre poke; the optogenetic epochs below start at cpoke_start_time or 0.65 s after it, which is consistent with the pulse train starting at the centre poke.

In [4]:
# Do the pulse columns, the correct side and the choice describe the same trials? Contrast the
# true pairing with each trial's pulses paired with the previous trial's side and choice.
rng = np.random.default_rng(1)
rows = []
for i in rng.choice(np.flatnonzero(S.selected), 200, replace=False):
    r = results[i]
    tr = r["trials"][r["trials"].hit.notna()].reset_index(drop=True)
    p = r["pulses"].sum(2).astype(int)                 # right_hi, left_hi, right_lo, left_lo
    loc = (p[:, 0] + p[:, 2]) - (p[:, 1] + p[:, 3])
    frq = (p[:, 0] + p[:, 1]) - (p[:, 2] + p[:, 3])
    rel = np.where(tr.task == "d", loc, frq)
    right = (tr.side == "r").values
    keep = rel != 0
    rows.append(dict(side_true=np.mean((rel[keep] > 0) == right[keep]),
                     side_shift=np.mean((rel[1:][keep[1:]] > 0) == right[:-1][keep[1:]]),
                     choice_true=np.mean((rel[keep] > 0) == (tr.choice.values[keep] == 1)),
                     choice_shift=np.mean((rel[1:][keep[1:]] > 0) == (tr.choice.values[:-1][keep[1:]] == 1)),
                     gdir_sign=np.mean(np.sign(loc[tr.gdir != 0]) == np.sign(tr.gdir[tr.gdir != 0]))))
chk = pd.DataFrame(rows)
print("200 selected sessions; fraction of valid trials (relevant pulse difference not 0) where:")
print(chk.describe().loc[["mean", "min", "max"]].round(3).to_string())

# Optogenetic epochs against the trial clock.
eps = []
for i, r in enumerate(results):
    if r["opto"] is not None and r["trials"] is not None:
        eps.append(ts.opto_trials(r["trials"], r["opto"]).assign(subject=S.subject[i], sid=i))
eps = pd.concat(eps, ignore_index=True)
print("\nOptogenetic epochs:", len(eps), "in", eps.sid.nunique(), "sessions of", sorted(eps.subject.unique()))
print("Epochs whose start falls inside a trial:", int(eps.in_trial.sum()))
print("Start minus cpoke_start_time (s), rounded:", eps.offset.round(3).value_counts().head(6).to_dict())
print("Epoch length (s):", eps.duration.value_counts().to_dict())
print("Sites:", eps.sites.value_counts().to_dict(), "| power (mW):", eps.power.value_counts().to_dict(),
      "| wavelength (nm):", eps.wavelength.value_counts().to_dict())

In selected sessions, the side with more relevant pulses is the stored correct side on every trial where the counts differ, and the choice follows the relevant pulses on most trials; paired with the previous trial instead, both fall to about one half. So the pulse columns, the correct side and the derived choice refer to the same trials, and the sign of the location pulse difference agrees with gamma_dir. Every optogenetic epoch starts inside a trial, at the centre poke or 0.65 s after it, and lasts 1.3 or 0.65 s, as the column description of opto_type says (full trial, first or second half). The files give the wavelength as 473 nm; Extended Data Figure 4 says 450 nm. Epochs are in four rats, where the paper reports three.

session-link¶

The dandiset's sessions can be linked to the paper's published per-session behavioural tables, and the linked records agree on trial counts, outcomes, evidence and pulse timing.

In [6]:
rng = np.random.default_rng(101)
rats = sorted(assets.subject.unique())
blobs = {}
with ThreadPoolExecutor(8) as ex:
    for rat, b in zip(rats, ex.map(lambda r: ts.paper_file(f"data/Sessions_trials/{r}_sessions.mat"), rats)):
        blobs[rat] = b
from scipy.io import loadmat
import io as _io
paper_rows = []
for rat in rats:
    m = loadmat(_io.BytesIO(blobs[rat]), squeeze_me=True, struct_as_record=False, variable_names=["sessions"])
    for k, s in enumerate(np.atleast_1d(m["sessions"])):
        paper_rows.append(dict(subject=rat, k=k, file=s.file, session=ts.paper_session_name(s.file),
                               valid_p=s.valid, hit_p=s.hit, good=s.good, bdir=s.bdir, bfreq=s.bfreq))
Pp = pd.DataFrame(paper_rows)
Pp["has_valid"] = Pp.valid_p.notna() & (Pp.valid_p > 0)
Pp["selected_p"] = (Pp.hit_p >= 0.7) & ((Pp.bdir + Pp.bfreq) / 2 >= 0.7) & (Pp.valid_p >= 100) & (Pp.good == 1)
M = Pp.merge(S[S.readable], on=["subject", "session"], how="outer", indicator=True)
print("Paper sessions:", len(Pp), "| with valid trials:", int(Pp.has_valid.sum()),
      "| found in the dandiset (readable):", int((M._merge == "both").sum()))
found = M[(M._merge != "right_only") & M.has_valid.fillna(False)]
frac_found = (found._merge == "both").mean()
print(f"Paper sessions with valid trials found in the dandiset: {frac_found:.4f}")
print("Paper sessions not found:", found.loc[found._merge == "left_only", ["subject", "session", "valid_p"]].to_string(index=False))
both = M[(M._merge == "both") & M.has_valid.fillna(False)]
eq_valid = (both.valid_p == both.valid).mean()
eq_hit = np.isclose(both.hit_p, both.hit).mean()
rel_ok = np.isclose(both.bdir, both.rel_loc, atol=1e-6) & np.isclose(both.bfreq, both.rel_frq, atol=1e-6)
print(f"Matched sessions: {len(both)}; valid trials equal in {eq_valid:.4f}, fraction correct equal in {eq_hit:.4f}, "
      f"both relative weights within 1e-6 in {rel_ok.mean():.4f}")
mis = both[~rel_ok]
capped_loc, capped_frq = np.minimum(mis.rel_loc, 1), np.minimum(mis.rel_frq, 1)
ok_capped = np.isclose(mis.bdir, capped_loc, atol=1e-6) & np.isclose(mis.bfreq, capped_frq, atol=1e-6)
print(f"\nSessions whose relative weights differ: {len(mis)}; of them equal once this attempt's values are capped at 1: "
      f"{int(ok_capped.sum())}; differing sessions that pass the paper's selection: {int(mis.selected_p.sum())}")
rest = mis[~ok_capped]
print("Differing after capping:", len(rest), "| with a missing value on either side:",
      int((rest[["bdir", "bfreq", "rel_loc", "rel_frq"]].isna().any(axis=1)).sum()),
      "| valid trials in them: median", rest.valid.median(), "max", rest.valid.max(),
      "| of them in the paper's selection:", int(rest.selected_p.sum()))
na_p = rest[["bdir", "bfreq"]].isna().any(axis=1)
na_d = rest[["rel_loc", "rel_frq"]].isna().any(axis=1)
print("Of them, missing in the paper's table only:", int((na_p & ~na_d).sum()), "| in this attempt's values only:",
      int((~na_p & na_d).sum()), "| on both sides:", int((na_p & na_d).sum()), "| on neither side:", int((~na_p & ~na_d).sum()))
print(rest[["subject", "session", "valid", "hit", "bdir", "rel_loc", "bfreq", "rel_frq"]].head(12).round(4).to_string(index=False))
both_present = rest[~na_p & ~na_d]
d = np.maximum(np.abs(both_present.bdir - np.minimum(both_present.rel_loc, 1)), np.abs(both_present.bfreq - np.minimum(both_present.rel_frq, 1)))
print(f"\nDiffering with both values present: {len(both_present)} | largest difference after capping: median {d.median():.4f}, "
      f"max {d.max():.4f} | valid trials: median {both_present.valid.median():.0f}, range {both_present.valid.min()} to {both_present.valid.max()} "
      f"| in the paper's selection: {int(both_present.selected_p.sum())}")
print("Their rats:", both_present.subject.value_counts().to_dict())
print(both_present.assign(diff=d)[["subject", "session", "valid", "hit", "bdir", "rel_loc", "bfreq", "rel_frq", "diff"]]
      .sort_values("diff", ascending=False).head(12).round(4).to_string(index=False))
only_d = M[M._merge == "right_only"]
print("\nTask sessions in the dandiset and not in the paper's tables:", len(only_d), "| of them pass the selection:",
      int(only_d.selected.sum()))
print(only_d[["subject", "session", "valid", "hit", "fsi", "selected"]].round(3).to_string(index=False))
extra = M[(M._merge == "both") & M.selected.astype(bool) & ~M.selected_p.fillna(False).astype(bool)]
print("\nSelected here, in the paper's tables, not selected there:")
print(extra[["subject", "session", "valid", "hit", "fsi", "valid_p", "hit_p", "good", "bdir", "bfreq", "rel_loc", "rel_frq"]].round(4).to_string(index=False))
xs = pd.crosstab(M.selected.fillna(False).rename("dandiset selection"), M.selected_p.fillna(False).rename("paper selection with good flag"))
print("\n", xs.to_string())

# Per-trial comparison on a seeded sample of 20 selected sessions found in both.
cand = M[(M._merge == "both") & M.selected & M.selected_p.fillna(False)]
sample = cand.iloc[rng.choice(len(cand), 20, replace=False)]
url_of = dict(zip(task_assets.subject + "/" + task_assets.session, task_assets.url))
rows = []
for _, row in sample.iterrows():
    tr_p = loadmat(_io.BytesIO(blobs[row.subject]), squeeze_me=True, struct_as_record=False,
                   variable_names=["trials"])["trials"][int(row.k)]
    d = ts.load_session(url_of[f"{row.subject}/{row.session}"], bin_s=0.01, n_bins=130, all_bins=True)
    tr = d["trials"][d["trials"].hit.notna()].reset_index(drop=True)
    p = d["pulses"].astype(int)
    mine = dict(vecr=p[:, 0] + p[:, 2], vecl=p[:, 1] + p[:, 3], vechi=p[:, 0] + p[:, 1], veclo=p[:, 2] + p[:, 3])
    n = len(tr)
    same_n = n == len(np.atleast_1d(tr_p.choice_all))
    agree = (same_n
             and np.array_equal(list(str(tr_p.task_all)), tr.task.tolist())
             and np.array_equal(list(str(tr_p.side_all)), tr.side.tolist()))
    per_trial = np.ones(n, bool) if same_n else np.zeros(n, bool)
    if same_n:
        per_trial &= np.array(list(str(tr_p.task_all))) == tr.task.values
        per_trial &= np.array(list(str(tr_p.side_all))) == tr.side.values
        per_trial &= np.isclose(tr_p.gdir_all, tr.gdir) & np.isclose(tr_p.gfreq_all, tr.gfreq)
        per_trial &= np.atleast_1d(tr_p.choice_all) == tr.choice.values
        per_trial &= np.atleast_1d(tr_p.hits_all) == tr.hit.values
        nta_eq = np.mean(np.atleast_1d(tr_p.nta_all) == tr.nta.values)
        bins_eq = np.mean([np.mean(getattr(tr_p, f"{k}_all") == mine[k]) for k in mine])
    else:
        nta_eq = bins_eq = np.nan
    rows.append(dict(subject=row.subject, session=row.session, trials=n, same_count=same_n,
                     trials_agree=per_trial.mean(), nta_agree=nta_eq, bins_10ms_agree=bins_eq))
sample_cmp = pd.DataFrame(rows)
print(sample_cmp.round(5).to_string(index=False))
print("\nOver the sample: trials agreeing on context, side, strengths, choice and outcome:",
      round(np.average(sample_cmp.trials_agree, weights=sample_cmp.trials), 5),
      "| position in block:", round(np.average(sample_cmp.nta_agree, weights=sample_cmp.trials), 5),
      "| 10 ms pulse bins:", round(np.average(sample_cmp.bins_10ms_agree, weights=sample_cmp.trials), 5))

# Every matched session, not only the sample: the per-trial fields, and the pulse counts in 50 ms
# bins (the paper's 10 ms bins summed in fives) for the sessions whose pulses were binned here.
idx_of = dict(zip(S.subject + "/" + S.session, S.index))
tot = dict(sessions=0, empty=0, same_count=0, trials=0, trials_agree=0, nta_agree=0, binned_trials=0, bins=0, bins_agree=0)
for rat in rats:
    trs = np.atleast_1d(loadmat(_io.BytesIO(blobs[rat]), squeeze_me=True, struct_as_record=False,
                                variable_names=["trials"])["trials"])
    for _, row in both[both.subject == rat].iterrows():
        i = idx_of[f"{rat}/{row.session}"]
        tr_p, tr = trs[int(row.k)], results[i]["trials"]
        tr = tr[tr.hit.notna()]
        n = len(tr)
        tot["sessions"] += 1
        if np.atleast_1d(tr_p.choice_all).size == 0:
            tot["empty"] += 1
            continue
        if n != np.atleast_1d(tr_p.choice_all).size:
            continue
        tot["same_count"] += 1
        ok = ((np.array(list(str(tr_p.task_all))) == tr.task.values) & (np.array(list(str(tr_p.side_all))) == tr.side.values)
              & np.isclose(np.atleast_1d(tr_p.gdir_all), tr.gdir) & np.isclose(np.atleast_1d(tr_p.gfreq_all), tr.gfreq)
              & (np.atleast_1d(tr_p.choice_all) == tr.choice.values) & (np.atleast_1d(tr_p.hits_all) == tr.hit.values))
        tot["trials"] += n; tot["trials_agree"] += int(ok.sum())
        tot["nta_agree"] += int((np.atleast_1d(tr_p.nta_all) == tr.nta.values).sum())
        if results[i]["pulses"] is not None:
            p = results[i]["pulses"].astype(int)
            mine = dict(vecr=p[:, 0] + p[:, 2], vecl=p[:, 1] + p[:, 3], vechi=p[:, 0] + p[:, 1], veclo=p[:, 2] + p[:, 3])
            for key, v in mine.items():
                theirs = np.asarray(getattr(tr_p, f"{key}_all")).reshape(n, -1).reshape(n, 26, 5).sum(2)
                tot["bins"] += v.size; tot["bins_agree"] += int((theirs == v).sum())
            tot["binned_trials"] += n
print(f"\nAll {tot['sessions']} matched sessions: {tot['empty']} have an empty per-trial record in the paper's tables; of the "
      f"other {tot['sessions'] - tot['empty']}, {tot['same_count']} have the same number of valid trials; over their "
      f"{tot['trials']} valid trials, context, side, strengths, choice and outcome agree on {tot['trials_agree'] / tot['trials']:.5f} "
      f"and position in block on {tot['nta_agree'] / tot['trials']:.5f}; over the {tot['binned_trials']} trials of the "
      f"sessions with binned pulses, 50 ms pulse bins agree on {tot['bins_agree'] / tot['bins']:.5f}")

cmp_hits["difference"] = cmp_hits.dandiset - cmp_hits.paper_numhits

print("Rats with equal counts:", int((cmp_hits.difference == 0).sum()), "of", len(cmp_hits))

Result: reproduced. Of the 15,278 paper sessions with valid trials, 15,277 (0.9999) are in the dandiset; the one missing (P189 TaskSwitch6-210516a) has 27 valid trials. In all 15,277 matched sessions the number of valid trials and the fraction correct are equal. In the 20 sampled sessions every valid trial agrees on context, correct side, strengths, choice and outcome, the position in block agrees on every trial, and 0.99996 of the 10 ms pulse bins agree. Over every matched session the same holds: 627 have an empty per-trial record in the paper's tables, and in the other 14,650 the valid trial counts are equal, the 7,447,692 valid trials agree on every per-trial field and on position in block (1.00000), and 0.99996 of the 50 ms pulse bins agree in the sessions whose pulses were binned (6,532,005 trials).

Both relative weights agree to 1e-6 in 0.898 of matched sessions. Of the 1,553 that differ, 861 agree once this attempt's values are capped at 1, which the paper's table does. Of the 692 left, 627 have a missing value on both sides and 5 in the paper's table only; the other 60 differ with both values present, by a median of 0.87 after capping (39 to 916 valid trials), and were not explained. The 12 largest of these differences are in sessions with a fraction correct of 0.34 to 0.69. Only 3 of the 692 are in the paper's selection. The Methods selection made from the dandiset alone keeps all 8,843 sessions the paper's code keeps, with its good flag, plus 6 more: 5 P187 and P189 sessions absent from the paper's tables, and P059 TaskSwitch4-170331a, where the location weight in the location context is 1.112 here and 1.0 in the paper's table, so its index falls to 0.697 there. The per-rat trial counts equal the paper's for 23 of 26 rats and exceed them by 213, 1,442 and 609 trials for P059, P187 and P189.

subjects¶

The study used 26 male Long-Evans rats, aged between 6 and 24 months.

Result: partially reproduced. The dandiset holds 26 subjects, all male Long Evans. Ages at the 8,849 selected sessions run from 3.0 to 39.1 months (median 15.4); 0.913 of sessions lie within the widened 5.4 to 26.4 months and 0.844 within 6 to 24. Eighteen rats have selected sessions before 5.4 months (the youngest at 3.0) and eight after 26.4 (P189 up to 39.1).

The dates of birth put 25 rats at 1.6 to 2.7 months at their first session in the dandiset (21 below 2 months), and 3.0 to 11.4 months at their first selected session. P189 is the exception: 14.1 months at its first session, which falls on the same day as P187's, whose date of birth is 2019-02-21 against P189's 2018-02-21. P189's date of birth may be a year early; with 2019-02-21 its first session would be at about 2.1 months. For the other rats the ages at the first session are those of rats that start training young, so the selected sessions below 6 months are likely real, and the Methods' 6 to 24 months does not describe them.

trials-per-session, blocks-per-session, session-duration¶

Rats performed on average 542 trials per session. On average, rats switched across 14.6 context blocks per session. Behavioural sessions lasted 2 to 4 hours.

Result: trials-per-session reproduced. Valid trials per session average 551.8 over the selected sessions (reading b) and 494.2 over all task sessions (reading d), both within 487.8 to 596.2; all trials average 817.9 and 749.7 (readings a and c), outside. The 13 unreadable sessions (1 to 3 trials) are left out of readings (c) and (d); added, they give 749.1 and 493.8.

Result: blocks-per-session reproduced. The number of switches averages 15.98 over the selected sessions and the number of blocks 13.90 over all task sessions, both within 13.14 to 16.06; blocks over selected sessions (16.98) and switches over all sessions (12.90) are outside.

Result: session-duration reproduced. The median duration is 2.50 h over the selected sessions and 2.57 h over all task sessions, within 1.8 to 4.4 h. Only 0.559 and 0.556 of sessions last 2 to 4 h, and 5% to 95% of selected sessions span 1.26 to 4.41 h.

ed1e-switch-four-trials¶

Rats switch the feature they attend to within about four trials of a new context block.

In [14]:
def switch_curves(mask, min_n=30):
    rows = []
    for rat in sorted(S.subject.unique()):
        ids = np.flatnonzero(mask & (S.subject == rat))
        if not len(ids):
            continue
        v = pd.concat([results[i]["trials"] for i in ids])
        v = v[v.hit.notna() & (v.block > 0)]
        for new in ("f", "d"):
            for k in range(1, 31):
                g = v[(v.task == new) & (v.nta == k)]
                if len(g) < min_n:
                    continue
                X = np.column_stack([np.ones(len(g)), g.gdir, g.gfreq])
                w = ts._irls(X, g.choice.values.astype(float))
                rel = w[2] / (w[1] + w[2]) if new == "f" else w[1] / (w[1] + w[2])
                rows.append(dict(rat=rat, new=new, k=k, rel=rel, n=len(g)))
    return pd.DataFrame(rows)


def switch_summary(c):
    m = c.groupby(["new", "k"]).rel.mean().unstack(0)
    plateau = m.loc[10:30].mean()
    return m, plateau

Behavioural kernels¶

The kernels of fig4-converging, fig4-loc-frq-uncorrelated, ed3g-halfsplit and fig5d-behaviour-neural are fitted here. The main fit uses the code's smoothness penalty with its weight chosen per rat and context by 3-fold cross-validation over 20, 200 and 2000; variants use the code's fixed 200, and for the recorded rats the code's looser selection (0.65 correct, 0.6 index). The cross-validation folds are drawn at random over trials, as the claims file fixes, so trials of one session can fall in different folds; this only affects which penalty weight is chosen, and the fixed-200 variant shows how much that matters for each claim.

In [16]:
def rat_data(rat, mask):
    X, y, task = [], [], []
    for i in np.flatnonzero(mask & (S.subject == rat)):
        r = results[i]
        if r["pulses"] is None:
            raise RuntimeError(f"pulses not kept for {S.session[i]}")
        tr = r["trials"][r["trials"].hit.notna()]
        X.append(ts.evidence_features(r["pulses"]))
        y.append(tr.choice.values)
        task.append(tr.task.values)
    return np.vstack(X), np.concatenate(y), np.concatenate(task)


rats100 = counts[counts >= 100000].index.tolist()
rats_fit = sorted(set(rats100) | set(ts.PAPER_EPHYS_RATS))
code_ephys_mask = S.readable & (S.valid >= 100) & (S.hit >= 0.65) & (S.fsi >= 0.6)
t0 = time.time()


def fit_rat(rat):
    seed = int(rat[1:]) + 1000                 # each rat's folds have their own seed
    X, y, task = rat_data(rat, S.selected)
    out = dict(rat=rat, n=len(y), main=ts.kernels(X, y, task, seed=seed))
    out["fixed200"] = ts.kernels(X, y, task, lam=200.0)
    if rat in rats100:
        halves = []
        for h in (0, 1):
            Xh, yh, th = [], [], []
            for ctx in ("d", "f"):
                idx = np.flatnonzero(task == ctx)
                cut = int(round(len(idx) / 2))
                part = idx[:cut] if h == 0 else idx[cut:]
                Xh.append(X[part]); yh.append(y[part]); th.append(task[part])
            Xh, yh, th = np.vstack(Xh), np.concatenate(yh), np.concatenate(th)
            halves.append((ts.kernels(Xh, yh, th, lam={c: out["main"][f"lam_{c}"] for c in "df"}),
                           ts.kernels(Xh, yh, th, lam=200.0)))
        out["halves"] = halves
    if rat in ts.PAPER_EPHYS_RATS:
        Xc, yc, tc = rat_data(rat, code_ephys_mask)
        out["code_sel_n"] = len(yc)
        out["code_sel_200"] = ts.kernels(Xc, yc, tc, lam=200.0)
        out["code_sel_cv"] = ts.kernels(Xc, yc, tc, seed=seed)
    return out


with ThreadPoolExecutor(4) as ex:
    fits = {f["rat"]: f for f in ex.map(fit_rat, rats_fit)}
print(f"fitted {len(fits)} rats in {time.time() - t0:.0f} s; every fit converged (a failed fit raises)")
print(pd.DataFrame({r: dict(trials=f["n"], lam_LOC=f["main"]["lam_d"], lam_FRQ=f["main"]["lam_f"])
                    for r, f in fits.items()}).T.to_string())

fig4-converging¶

Differential behavioural kernels predominantly converge towards the end of the pulse train, that is the difference between contexts in the weight of a feature shrinks for later pulses.

fig4-loc-frq-uncorrelated¶

Across rats, the shape of the differential behavioural kernel for one feature does not predict the shape for the other feature.

In [19]:
def pearson_ci(a, b):
    r, p = stats.pearsonr(a, b)
    z, se = np.arctanh(r), 1 / np.sqrt(len(a) - 3)
    return r, p, np.tanh(z - 1.96 * se), np.tanh(z + 1.96 * se)


for a, b, name in (("loc", "frq", "main"), ("loc_200", "frq_200", "fixed 200"), ("loc_paper_weights", "frq_paper_weights", "paper's saved weights")):
    r, p, lo, hi = pearson_ci(sl[a], sl[b])
    print(f"{name}: r = {r:.3f} (95% CI {lo:.3f} to {hi:.3f}), p = {p:.3g}, n = {len(sl)}")

main: r = 0.180 (95% CI -0.313 to 0.597), p = 0.475, n = 18
fixed 200: r = 0.092 (95% CI -0.392 to 0.536), p = 0.717, n = 18
paper's saved weights: r = 0.094 (95% CI -0.390 to 0.537), p = 0.71, n = 18

Result: reproduced. Across the 18 rats the location and frequency slope indices are not significantly correlated: r = 0.180 (95% CI -0.313 to 0.597), p = 0.475; with the fixed penalty r = 0.092, p = 0.717.

ed4-bilateral-fof-impairs¶

Bilateral optogenetic silencing of the frontal orienting fields during the stimulus impairs performance of the task (three rats).

In [21]:
rows = []
opto_sessions = S[S.readable & (S.valid >= 100)].index.intersection(eps.sid.unique())
for i in opto_sessions:
    tr = results[i]["trials"].reset_index(drop=True)
    e = eps[(eps.sid == i) & eps.in_trial]
    lab = pd.Series("control", index=tr.index, dtype=object)
    for _, ep in e.iterrows():
        lab[ep.trial] = f"{ep.sites}_{ep.window}"
    tr = tr.assign(cond=lab.values)
    tr = tr[tr.hit.notna()]
    rows.append(tr.assign(subject=S.subject[i]))
ot = pd.concat(rows, ignore_index=True)

print(tab["mean"].round(3).to_string()); print(tab["size"].fillna(0).astype(int).to_string())
top3 = n_sessions.sort_values(ascending=False).index[:3].tolist()
res_rows = []
for rat in n_sessions.index:
    g = ot[ot.subject == rat]
    ctl = g[g.cond == "control"].hit
    for name, cond in (("full", g.cond == "bilateral_full"), ("any", g.cond.str.startswith("bilateral"))):
        b = g[cond].hit
        if len(b) == 0:
            res_rows.append(dict(rat=rat, epochs=name, n_bilateral=0)); continue
        table = [[int(b.sum()), int(len(b) - b.sum())], [int(ctl.sum()), int(len(ctl) - ctl.sum())]]
        p = stats.fisher_exact(table)[1]
        res_rows.append(dict(rat=rat, epochs=name, n_bilateral=len(b), acc_bilateral=b.mean(), n_control=len(ctl),
                             acc_control=ctl.mean(), difference=b.mean() - ctl.mean(), p=p))

Result: partially reproduced. Four rats have optogenetic sessions, where the paper reports three. With bilateral full-trial epochs, accuracy is lower than on control trials of the same sessions with p < 0.05 in 2 of the 3 rats with the most opto sessions: P116 (0.639 against 0.733, p below 1e-4) and P131 (0.686 against 0.727, p = 0.0001). P124 is higher (0.712 against 0.687, p = 0.17), and P127 is lower but not significantly (4 sessions, 0.603 against 0.634, p = 0.55). Any bilateral epoch gives the same counts. Every trial with an epoch has the laser connected, and the few control trials without it change nothing: with laser-connected trials only, P116, P124 and P131 give the same accuracies and p values.

neural-link, units-per-rat¶

The neurons in the paper's published neural data can be linked to the dandiset's rats and sessions; they come from 199 sessions of 7 rats. The recordings yielded 3,495 putative single units, 2,047, 832, 258, 94 and 54 from five rats in FOF and 112 and 98 from two rats in mPFC.

In [22]:
t0 = time.time()
rat_numbers = ts.paper_mat("data/rat_for_each_neuron.mat")["rat_numbers"].astype(int)
n_cells = len(rat_numbers)


def read_cell(n):
    m = ts.paper_mat(f"data/neural_data/cell_{n}.mat", variable_names=["behav", "rat_name", "brain_region"])
    b = m["behav"]
    return dict(cell=n, rat=str(m["rat_name"]), region=str(m["brain_region"]), n_trials=int(b.nTrials),
                sym=ts.trial_symbols(list(str(b.task)), np.atleast_1d(b.gdir), np.atleast_1d(b.gfreq), np.atleast_1d(b.choice)))

# Each rat's valid trials, session by session, as one string; a cell matches where its trials appear.
sym_sessions = {}
for i, r in enumerate(results):
    if r["trials"] is None or S.subject[i] not in ts.PAPER_EPHYS_RATS:
        continue
    v = r["trials"][r["trials"].hit.notna()]
    sym_sessions.setdefault(S.subject[i], []).append((S.session[i], ts.trial_symbols(v.task, v.gdir, v.gfreq, v.choice)))
matches = []
for _, c in cells.iterrows():
    found = [sid for sid, s in sym_sessions.get(c.rat, []) if c.sym and c.sym in s]
    matches.append(found)
cells["n_match"] = [len(f) for f in matches]
cells["session"] = [f[0] if len(f) == 1 else None for f in matches]
print("Rats of the neural data in the dandiset:", sorted(set(cells.rat) & set(assets.subject)))
print("Cells matching exactly one session:", int((cells.n_match == 1).sum()), "of", len(cells),
      f"({(cells.n_match == 1).mean():.4f}); none: {int((cells.n_match == 0).sum())}; more than one: {int((cells.n_match > 1).sum())}")
print("Distinct matched sessions:", cells.session.nunique(), "| per rat:", cells.groupby("rat").session.nunique().to_dict())
print("Cells without a match, per rat:", cells[cells.n_match == 0].groupby("rat").size().to_dict(),
      "| their trial counts:", cells[cells.n_match == 0].n_trials.describe()[["min", "50%", "max"]].to_dict())
print("Matched sessions by protocol:", pd.Series([s.split("-")[0] for s in cells.session.dropna().unique()]).value_counts().to_dict())
print("Paper: 199 sessions (tolerance 179.1 to 218.9)")

# Variant: the cell's trials as an ordered subsequence of one session's valid trials (gaps allowed).
gap = [m if m else ts.gap_match(c.sym, sym_sessions.get(c.rat, [])) for m, (_, c) in zip(matches, cells.iterrows())]
cells["n_gap"] = [len(g) for g in gap]
cells["session_gap"] = [g[0] if len(g) == 1 else None for g in gap]
print("\nVariant, gaps allowed: cells matching exactly one session", int((cells.n_gap == 1).sum()), "of", len(cells),
      f"({(cells.n_gap == 1).mean():.4f}); none: {int((cells.n_gap == 0).sum())}; more than one: {int((cells.n_gap > 1).sum())}")
print("Distinct sessions:", cells.session_gap.nunique(), "| per rat:", cells.groupby("rat").session_gap.nunique().to_dict())
unm = cells[cells.n_gap == 0]
print("Cells still unmatched, per rat:", unm.groupby("rat").size().to_dict())

# Variant: every TaskSwitch protocol of the recorded rats, adding TaskSwitch4repeat and others.
sym_all = {k: list(v) for k, v in sym_sessions.items()}
for i, r in enumerate(other_results):
    if r["trials"] is None or other_assets.subject[i] not in ts.PAPER_EPHYS_RATS:
        continue
    v = r["trials"][r["trials"].hit.notna()]
    sym_all[other_assets.subject[i]].append((other_assets.session[i], ts.trial_symbols(v.task, v.gdir, v.gfreq, v.choice)))
print("\nSessions searched per rat, three task protocols:", {k: len(v) for k, v in sym_sessions.items()},
      "| every TaskSwitch protocol:", {k: len(v) for k, v in sym_all.items()})
m_all = [[sid for sid, s in sym_all.get(c.rat, []) if c.sym and c.sym in s] for _, c in cells.iterrows()]
g_all = [m if m else ts.gap_match(c.sym, sym_all.get(c.rat, [])) for m, (_, c) in zip(m_all, cells.iterrows())]
cells["n_match_all"] = [len(f) for f in m_all]
cells["n_gap_all"] = [len(f) for f in g_all]
cells["session_all"] = [f[0] if len(f) == 1 else None for f in m_all]
cells["session_gap_all"] = [f[0] if len(f) == 1 else None for f in g_all]
for col, name in (("n_match_all", "contiguous"), ("n_gap_all", "gaps allowed")):
    sess_col = "session_all" if col == "n_match_all" else "session_gap_all"
    print(f"Every TaskSwitch protocol, {name}: cells matching exactly one session {int((cells[col] == 1).sum())} "
          f"({(cells[col] == 1).mean():.4f}); none {int((cells[col] == 0).sum())}; more than one {int((cells[col] > 1).sum())}; "
          f"distinct sessions {cells[sess_col].nunique()}")
print("Sessions matched (gaps allowed) by protocol:", pd.Series([s.split("-")[0] for s in cells.session_gap_all.dropna().unique()]).value_counts().to_dict())

# Per rat: cells, matches, sessions and the dates of the matched sessions (every TaskSwitch protocol).
cells["date_all"] = cells.session_gap_all.str[-7:-1]
per_rat_cells = cells.groupby("rat").agg(
    cells=("cell", "size"), contiguous=("n_match_all", lambda x: int((x == 1).sum())),
    gaps_allowed=("n_gap_all", lambda x: int((x == 1).sum())), unmatched=("n_gap_all", lambda x: int((x == 0).sum())),
    sessions_contiguous=("session_all", "nunique"), sessions_gaps=("session_gap_all", "nunique"),
    first_date=("date_all", "min"), last_date=("date_all", "max"), trials_median=("n_trials", "median"))
per_rat_cells["unmatched_trials_median"] = cells[cells.n_gap_all == 0].groupby("rat").n_trials.median()
print(per_rat_cells.to_string())

# The cells that match no session: how much of each falls inside one dandiset session. Their
# trials are cut into windows of 8, and the share of windows found in the best session is given.
rows = []
for _, c in cells[cells.n_gap_all == 0].iterrows():
    w = [c.sym[k:k + 8] for k in range(0, len(c.sym) - 7, 8)]
    best = max((np.mean([x in s for x in w]), sid) for sid, s in sym_all[c.rat])
    rows.append(dict(rat=c.rat, trials=c.n_trials, share=best[0], session=best[1]))
unm_all = pd.DataFrame(rows)
print(f"\nUnmatched cells: {len(unm_all)}; share of their 8-trial windows found in their best session: median "
      f"{unm_all.share.median():.2f}, range {unm_all.share.min():.2f} to {unm_all.share.max():.2f}; "
      f"best sessions not among those matched: {len(set(unm_all.session) - set(cells.session_gap_all.dropna()))} "
      f"of {unm_all.session.nunique()}")

Result: neural-link not reproduced. The seven rats are in the dandiset and every cell names one of them, but only 2,371 of 3,495 cells (0.678) have trials equal to a contiguous run of one session's valid trials, from 110 distinct sessions against the paper's 199 (tolerance 179 to 219). With gaps allowed (the variant), 3,269 cells (0.935) match exactly one session and none matches more than one, so the neural files leave out some of a session's valid trials and the rule chosen here is stricter than the data need; but these cells still come from only 112 dandiset sessions, and 226 cells, 189 of them P100's, match none.

Searching every TaskSwitch protocol of the recorded rats (adding P100's 13 TaskSwitch4repeat sessions) raises the contiguous matches to 2,425 (0.694) and the matches with gaps to 3,349 (0.958), from 113 and 115 sessions; 3 of the new sessions are TaskSwitch4repeat. The 146 cells still unmatched share a median of 0.43 of their 8-trial windows with their best session, and all but 3 of those best sessions are among the 115 already matched, so they do not point to missing sessions. Per rat the matched sessions are 6, 10, 10, 39, 75, 28 and 26, recorded from February 2018 to July 2019. Under no search does the number of sessions approach 199.

Result: units-per-rat reproduced. The cell files hold 3,495 units, 3,285 in FOF (2,047, 832, 258, 94 and 54 in P100, P059, P055, P095 and P049) and 210 in mPFC (112 in P101 and 98 in P102), as the Methods' per-rat counts say. The Methods' "3,495 ... recorded from 5 rats in FOF" counts the mPFC units as well.

fig3h-neural-uncorrelated, choice-axes-parallel¶

Neural slope indices vary across rats and features, with no apparent correlation between the location and frequency indices across the seven recorded rats. Choice axes estimated separately in the two contexts are essentially parallel (average angle 1.6 degrees).

Result: reproduced. The neural location and frequency slope indices from the paper's fitted kernels are not significantly correlated across the seven rats (r = -0.177, 95% CI -0.821 to 0.665, p = 0.704), and they vary: location -0.221 to 1.728, frequency 0.465 to 1.500. The Methods say the differential pulse responses "only displayed positive (or zero) slope indices"; three location indices are negative here, P049 -0.221, P101 -0.045 and P095 -0.007. The claim's criterion does not test this.

Result: not reproduced. ExtDataFigure5ag.m computes two angles and plots the second: the two context choice axes projected on the first 3 principal components of both contexts' choice kernels (which explain 0.85 to 0.94 of their variance), folded to at most 90 degrees. On the paper's own fitted per-context kernels these angles are 1.12 to 8.00 degrees (P100 1.12, P095 1.82, P101 4.25, P059 4.49, P049 5.53, P055 7.91, P102 8.00), mean 4.73, against the paper's 1.6 (tolerance 1.44 to 1.76); no rat lies in the tolerance and one lies below it. The angle in the full space, which the code computes first and then overwrites, is 13.4 to 128.2 degrees, mean 40.3 (29.4 folded). The axes are close to parallel in the 3-dimensional space but not as close as reported. The paper's test of each angle against 0 ("not different from 0 in 6 of 7 rats") is the permutation test the Methods describe under "Estimating the choice axis": the context labels of the trials are shuffled and the axes recomputed. It is not in the repository's code and needs the per-neuron kernels refitted for every shuffle, so it was not run.

fig5d-behaviour-neural¶

The behavioural slope index and the neural slope index are anti-correlated across rats and features (r = -0.73, P < 0.01), and for location (r = -0.71) and frequency (r = -0.71) alone (P < 0.1).

Result: reproduced. Between the behavioural slope index from the dandiset (Methods selection, second half of the stimulus) and the neural slope index from the paper's kernels, r = -0.697 over 14 values (95% CI -0.896 to -0.264), p = 0.0056, within -0.803 to -0.657. For location alone r = -0.675 (p = 0.096) and for frequency alone r = -0.772 (p = 0.042). With the code's selection and penalty r = -0.765 (p = 0.0014), and the paper's own saved behavioural indices give -0.768.

The result is close to the edge of the tolerance and rests on two rats with few trials. P049 and P059 have 23,014 and 25,847 trials under the Methods selection against 135,001 and 162,317 under the code's, and their location indices change sign between the two (0.131 against -0.432; 1.292 against -0.613). Taking those two rats from the code's selection gives r = -0.834, and the code's selection with the cross-validated penalty r = -0.830, both more negative than the tolerance. Leaving out one rat at a time gives -0.655 to -0.895, inside the tolerance for 4 of 7 rats. The five 14-point correlations printed above are all negative with p < 0.01.

How the analysis differs from the paper's. The session selection is the Methods' (the code's extra good flag is not in the dandiset, and never removes a session that passes the other criteria). The feature selection index uses the stored generative log rate ratios; the relative weights equal the paper's per-session values to 1e-6 in 0.898 of matched sessions, 861 more agree once capped at 1 as the paper's table does, 627 are missing on both sides, and 60 differ with both values present. The behavioural kernels use the code's smoothness penalty, read as the Methods' "ridge regression", with its weight chosen by 3-fold cross-validation over 20, 200 and 2000 (grid and folds chosen here); the code's fixed 200 is shown as a variant and gives slope indices within 0.018 of those from the paper's saved weights. For the recorded rats the Methods selection keeps far fewer trials of P049 and P059 than the code's looser one, which is shown as a variant. Several numbers in the Methods (trials and blocks per session, session length) do not say which sessions or trials they count; the readings are listed in the claims file. The neural claims use the paper's fitted per-neuron kernels from its GitHub repository, not a refit from spikes. The choice-axis angle is the one ExtDataFigure5ag.m plots, in the space of the first 3 principal components of both contexts' choice kernels. The mTDR and RNN analyses were not run.

What was found about the dandiset. It holds the behaviour of all 26 rats and links to the paper's published per-session tables: 15,277 of 15,278 paper sessions with valid trials are in it, with equal valid trial counts and fraction correct, and 6 dandiset task sessions are not in the tables. In the 14,650 matched sessions with a per-trial record in the paper's tables every valid trial agrees on context, side, strengths, choice and outcome, and 0.99996 of 50 ms pulse bins agree; 627 have no per-trial record there to compare. The paper's trial selection can be rebuilt from the dandiset alone, adding 6 sessions. It does not hold the electrophysiology, which is only in the paper's GitHub repository, as MATLAB files per cell with no session identifier; most cells can be placed in a dandiset session only by matching their trial sequences. The optogenetic epochs state 473 nm where the paper says 450 nm, and are present in four rats where the paper reports three, without saying which three were analysed. Dates of birth give ages of 3 to 39 months at the analysed sessions, where the Methods say 6 to 24; they put 25 rats at 1.6 to 2.7 months at their first session, and P189's date of birth looks a year early. Thirteen task sessions lack the result codes or a pulse column, and one paper session with 27 valid trials is not in the dandiset. The cells of the paper's neural files match 110 dandiset sessions as contiguous runs of trials and 112 with gaps allowed (113 and 115 when every TaskSwitch protocol is searched), not the 199 the paper reports, and 146 to 226 match none. The choice-axis angles computed from the paper's own kernels by its own code average 4.7 degrees, not the 1.6 it reports.
